A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Group|group]], $H$ a [[Definition:Subgroup|subgroup]] and $N$ a [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroup]] of $G$.
Then:
:$H N / N \cong H / \paren {H \cap N}$

B_source.statement:
Let $i: H \to G$ be an [[Definition:Inclusion Mapping|inclusion]] and $q: G \to G / N$ a [[Definition:Quotient Epimorphism|quotient map]].
Then $q \circ i$ is a [[Definition:Surjection|surjection]] onto its image, with [[Definition:Kernel of Group Homomorphism|kernel]] $\map {i^{-1} } {\map \ker q}$.

substitutions.the composite map: the inclusion of H into HN followed by the quotient by N
substitutions.the image of the composite: the whole of HN modulo N
substitutions.the kernel of the composite: the elements of H lying in N, that is, the intersection

derived.surjectivity of the composite: every class in HN modulo N has a representative in H

validity_conditions: The product set HN is a subgroup because N is normal, so the second map is defined on it.
The composite is surjective since any element of HN is a product of an element of H with one of N, and the second factor dies in the quotient.
The kernel of the composite consists of elements of H that lie in N, which is exactly the intersection, and that intersection is normal in H.
proof_plan: Let $\phi = q \circ i: H \to G / N$, $\map \phi h = h N$.

For $h n \in H N$, $h n N = h N = \map \phi h$.
Hence $\phi$ is [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] onto $H N / N$.

We have:
:$\map \ker \phi = \set {h \in H: h N = N} = H \cap N$

By the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]]:
:$H / \paren {H \cap N} \cong H N / N$
which is the [[Second Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]].
{{qed}}
